lines.speaker: Caelan
lines.text: I need to close it. The threshold. That's what I'm for.
lines.monologue: He said 'what I'm for' without sadness. Like a door understanding its purpose. Not diminished by it. Defined.

lines.speaker: Caelan
lines.text: I don't think so. I think it will feel like remembering.
lines.monologue: He looked at each of them. Not goodbye. Just... seeing them. Making sure he'd remember this part. The small part. The human part.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Caelan stepped forward and for a moment he was what he had been — vast, between, neither here nor there. The chamber filled with light that was also absence. Every person in the room felt the edges of something too large for perception.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He chose to be Caelan again. Small. Named. Forgetting. The threshold sealed behind him like water closing over a stone.

lines.speaker: Rynn
lines.monologue: The pressure dropped. The air tasted like air again. Her ears popped, the way they do when you descend from altitude.

lines.speaker: Lex
lines.text: It's not gone. The damage. The corruption that already spread — it's still there.
lines.monologue: He was right. What was damaged stayed damaged. But it wasn't growing anymore. The tide had stopped.

lines.speaker: Suri
lines.text: Then we rebuild the routes around it. Map what's lost. Start from what's left.
lines.monologue: She was already calculating. New routes. New trade lines. The cost of rebuilding versus the cost of starting over. She would choose the one that fed more people.

lines.speaker: Rynn
lines.text: I can map the safe paths. It'll take weeks but the forest will tell me where the ground is solid.
lines.monologue: She'd already started. In her head she was walking the Ereivyn canopy, reading the bark for signs of health, counting the birds that hadn't come back yet.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The next morning. The camp. Breakfast.

lines.speaker: Lex
lines.text: I'm going to write about what happened. No one will believe it. That's fine. The archivists three hundred years ago stopped writing. I won't.
lines.monologue: He opened a new notebook. The first line was: 'This is what happened, as best as one person can describe a thing that is larger than description.'

lines.speaker: Caelan
lines.monologue: He was eating bread. Slowly. Tasting it. He still didn't remember everything. He was okay with that now. Some things are better left as shapes in water.

lines.speaker: Zi
lines.lens: He's eating. His hands are steady. His color is good. His breathing is even.
lines.monologue: She watched him eat breakfast and didn't say anything. There was nothing to say. He was here. He chose to be here. That was enough.

lines.speaker: Suri
lines.monologue: She asked it the way she always did. Offering without being asked. Probably didn't think of it as kindness. It was.
